source_text: Randomized trials demonstrate that male circumcision decreases heterosexual HIV acquisition by 53-60% and lowers transmission risks for herpes simplex virus type 2 and human papillomavirus, thereby protecting uncircumcised partners and reducing overall community STI prevalence without relying solely on individual behavioral changes.
